evals.name: favorites-panel
evals.prompt: Add a favorites feature to the tourist map: a small heart-shaped toggle button on the POI detail card that saves/removes that POI from a favorites list (kept in local component state for now, no backend needed), and a new floating panel opened from the bottom menu that lists the saved favorites and lets you jump back to a POI's detail. Implement it in apps/tourist-web.
evals.expected_output: New floating panel and toggle button implemented as real code changes in apps/tourist-web, reusing the app's existing floating-overlay/pill visual language (radius, shadow, color, 44px targets) instead of inventing a new style; the new panel is placed correctly in the established z-index/layering stack; the heart toggle uses aria-pressed (genuine toggle state) with a focus-visible ring matching existing controls; the new panel follows the 'CSS adapts, markup doesn't fork' responsive convention (one markup tree, breakpoint override) rather than a separate mobile component.
expectations: New CSS for the favorites panel/button uses an existing radius token (999px pill, 12px card, or 16px 16px 0 0 mobile sheet) rather than an arbitrary new radius value
The new floating panel's elevation uses an existing shadow token (0 4px 16px rgba(0,0,0,0.2) or 0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.15))
The heart toggle button has a 44px (or larger) min-width/min-height tap target even if visually smaller
The heart toggle button carries aria-pressed reflecting saved/not-saved state
Any new responsive behavior for the favorites panel is added inside the existing 640px overlay breakpoint rather than introducing a new breakpoint
New interactive controls participate in the shared focus-visible outline styling rather than defining a one-off focus style
The new panel is positioned as an absolutely-positioned overlay inside the existing map body, not a new full-page route

evals.name: poi-extra-fields
evals.prompt: Update the POI detail card in apps/tourist-web so it also shows opening hours and a contact phone number, similar to what you'd see in a Google Maps info window.
evals.expected_output: The agent checks whether opening hours / phone actually exist on the PublishedPoi snapshot type (shared-types) before rendering them. Since neither field exists on that type today, the correct outcome is NOT hardcoding/inventing fake data for them — either the fields are added properly end-to-end (snapshot type + publish pipeline + component) if that's in scope, or the agent explains the fields aren't available in the current published snapshot and stops short of faking them, rather than rendering placeholder/hardcoded values.
expectations: The summary/output shows the agent actually looked at the PublishedPoi type in shared-types before deciding what to do
The diff does not render a hardcoded/fake opening-hours or phone-number string as if it were real POI data
The diff does not add a disabled/non-functional button implying a capability (e.g. 'Call', 'Hours') that isn't backed by real data
If the agent chose not to implement the fields, it explains why (fields absent from the published snapshot type) rather than silently doing nothing or silently faking it

evals.name: search-mobile-fix
evals.prompt: A few tourists said the search overlay is annoying on their phones — the close button feels too small to tap accurately and it's hard to tell it's focused. Fix the search overlay's mobile usability in apps/tourist-web.
evals.expected_output: The close button already has a 44x44px hit target and a shared focus-visible outline in the current code (apps/tourist-web/app/globals.css) — the correct fix identifies what's actually still wrong (e.g. visual affordance, spacing, or a genuine mobile-only issue) rather than re-deriving the touch-target/focus-ring rules from scratch or duplicating them as new one-off CSS instead of reusing/extending the existing shared rules.
expectations: The summary/output shows the agent recognized the close button already has a 44px target rather than re-adding one from scratch
The summary/output shows the agent recognized the shared focus-visible outline already exists rather than writing a duplicate one-off focus rule
The diff does not introduce a new, separate CSS rule that duplicates logic already centralized in the shared focus-visible selector list

The fix targets something plausibly still wrong (e.g. visual size/affordance of the glyph, hit-area spacing near other controls, or an actual mobile-only regression) rather than a no-op restatement of existing CSS
